correctness.rationale: For all commutative k-algebras R in characteristic two, independent generator coefficient variables yield exactly \(a_i^2=0\) and \(\det L\) invertible; invertibility across the nilpotent ideal \((a_i)\) proves the full coordinate scheme and smooth reduction. In odd characteristic, the quadratic coefficient comparison forces monomial cotangent images, while the decomposition \(B\oplus x_jB\) forces \(x_j\) times a unique unit. Thus all components and both finite-field orders follow. Tangent spaces are Der(A), dimensions \(d2^d\) in char2 and \(d2^{d-1}\) otherwise; the char2 scheme is nonreduced by the \(\alpha_2\) factor and char!=2 scheme is smooth by its reduced geometric dimension/tangent equality. All six independent finite-field enumerations and tangent calculations passed; these are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Novelty is restricted to the uniform characteristic-two nonreduced automorphism scheme, tangent-excess comparison, and exact finite-field group orders as a package. The 1997 graded and 2024 characteristic-zero automorphism work covers significant slices and is acknowledged. The 2012 paper covers K-theory of the same ring and the closest published arbitrary-field automorphism result addresses a different coordinate-cross quotient. No inspected equivalent scheme theorem was found; modular group algebra coverage is an explicit residual risk, and no claim of certified historical priority is made.
residual_risks: The modular group algebra \(k[(C_2)^d]\) is isomorphic to this A_d in characteristic two; general automorphism-scheme treatments may implicitly contain the result.
Small-field group-order special cases are known and not novel by themselves.
Full formal publication-priority coverage across all monomial-ring and Hopf/group-algebra terminology is not proven.
The earliest known-year 1997 source lacks a verified first-public calendar day in the evidence set; the dated 2012 source is used for cohort qualification.

value.rationale: The automorphism group scheme is an intrinsic invariant of finite-dimensional commutative complete intersections. The \(\alpha_2\) infinitesimal directions give a uniform nonsmoothness theorem with exact dimension excess d, rather than an isolated point count. The connected versus \(d!\)-component, \(\mathrm{GL}_d\) versus monomial-linear characteristic transition and exact orders for all finite fields describe nontrivial structural boundaries across unbounded embedding dimension. The relationship to grading-preserving/Poisson-preserving subgroups and existing characteristic-zero theory is acknowledged.
